options.text: The company let the investors elect their own king to rule the new colony
options.misconception: No colony elected a king; the colonies answered to the crown that granted the charter.

options.text: The company let the crown give up all authority over the colonies it granted
options.misconception: Reverses the charter; the crown kept authority over the colonies and a share of their wealth.

options.text: The company let many investors share the cost and risk of a venture few could afford
The company let the investors avoid all risk by guaranteeing a profit on every voyage
options.misconception: Nothing guaranteed a profit; the risk was real, and early colonies like Roanoke failed outright.

rationales.general:
1. Picture a colony bought the way a crowd funds a project. Ships, supplies, and settlers cost more than one investor could pay.
2. Ask what the risk was. The colony might fail, as Roanoke had, and the money would be lost.
3. Ask what the company did. It spread the cost and the risk across many shareholders.
4. Rule out the others. The crown kept authority, no king was elected, and no profit was guaranteed.
Remember: when a venture is costly and risky, ask who shares the bill.
rationales.C: A colony cost more than any one investor could pay, and the risk of failure was high. Sharing the cost across many investors made the venture possible.
rationales.A: No colony elected a king. The colonies answered to the crown that granted the charter.
rationales.B: The charter kept authority with the crown, which also took a share of any wealth found. The crown gave up nothing.
rationales.D: No profit was guaranteed. The risk was real, and early colonies like Roanoke failed outright.

stem: The First Charter of Virginia (1606) gave English investors the right to plant colonies through a joint-stock company, with the crown keeping authority and a share of any wealth found. Which of the following best explains why England used a joint-stock company to plant colonies?

stimulus.source_note: First Charter of Virginia, granted by King James I, April 1606; title page from Select Charters (Macmillan, 1899), public domain.
stimulus.text: The First Charter of Virginia, granted by King James I in April 1606, gave two groups of English investors the right to plant colonies on the American coast. The charter created a joint-stock company: investors bought shares, and the company used the money to pay for ships, supplies, and settlers. The crown kept authority over the colonies and took a share of any gold, silver, or other wealth found.
